approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic algorithm over molecular graphs with a Bayesian batch allocator on top, and it never sees the objective it is optimizing. Each objective runs as a fresh process with ten scored starting molecules and a budget of 300 oracle calls, answered ten molecules at a time. It keeps the best 64 scored molecules it has seen as a breeding population, draws parents preferentially from the top score quantiles, and builds each child either by cutting a single bond in each of two parents and joining the pieces (with a 45 per cent chance, and a 35 per cent chance of one finishing edit afterwards) or by walking one to three small edits over a single parent - swap an atom's element, hang one atom on, delete an atom, splice an atom into a bond, change a bond order, close a ring, open a ring - with a longer walk forced when the batch has been failing to produce anything new. Every candidate must be a connected, valence-legal molecule whose canonical identity round-trips, must be new to this session, and must not introduce an unusual sulfur environment that none of its own parents had. It breeds 160 such candidates per batch, scores them with a Gaussian process fitted only on this session's accepted molecules using a Morgan-count Tanimoto kernel, and picks the ten to evaluate by drawing correlated samples from that posterior and taking the sampled maximum ten times, masking out each pick as it goes. The one mechanism earlier work added on top of this is a stall response: after three consecutive batches that fail to beat the best molecule so far, only the forty highest posterior means stay eligible for those draws, and the full field returns on the first improving batch.
approach.novelty: I give this generator the one move it has never had: a step whose unit is a whole piece of chemistry rather than one atom or bond. Before each breeding attempt, with a declared probability of 0.30, the parent either receives a complete ring system or a small functional group at an explicitly chosen attachment point, or has one of its own complete ring systems or side chains cut out and a drawn one put in its place - one accepted step, one whole unit. The units come from a vocabulary mined once, offline, from the permitted unlabeled corpus by frequency alone: every ring system and every small acyclic side chain that occurs in more than a thousand corpus molecules. I ran that extraction over the whole corpus before writing this plan, so the vocabulary is a measured object rather than a hope: 216 units, 134 of them whole ring systems, and among them exactly the pieces this generator has provably never produced - trifluoromethyl, tetrazole and nitro, none of which appears in any of the 4,500 trajectory records the Parent has. The vocabulary never reads a score, a task identity or an oracle answer, no corpus molecule ever enters a pool or an evaluation, and everything else stays exactly as inherited - the seven atom and bond operators at their weights, the crossover and its finishing edit, the admission rules, the surrogate and the stall response - so the repertoire is extended rather than replaced and the new products are priced by the allocator the Anchor already uses. Two coarse-chemistry attempts have been made on this lineage before, and this differs from both in three stated ways rather than in wording. Both of them took the place of an existing operator - one substituted the entire seven-edit mutation neighbourhood with a context-matched fragment replacement at a witnessed single cut, the other substituted the crossover constructor with a BRICS-label-compatible single cut between the two scored parents - and both lost, by -0.044 and -0.095 of the panel mean, while removing the crossover alone costs between -0.014 and -0.055 across three Parents; this move is added, and takes a share of attempts rather than a component's place. Both also needed a cut and a compatible context before they could put anything in: this move can simply hang a whole unit on a free valence, and when it does exchange, it chooses the incoming unit by global corpus frequency with no reference to the site it lands on, so the unit is not constrained to what the host's local environment already matches. And both were measured on the previous, mask-free Parent, whereas the structural numbers this one is pre-registered against are recomputed on this Anchor's own fifteen sessions. It is also not the refuted refinement stage, which locally re-decorated ready-made corpus continuations and assembled no ring system at all. The three siblings planned beside it this round touch the surrogate's prior variance, the measurement scale and the admission rules, and leave the proposal operators byte-identical.

observed_bottleneck: Every proposal move this Anchor owns is atom- or bond-local except one connected-fragment crossover, so no single accepted step can bring in a multi-atom group or a complete ring system that is not already sitting in one of the two generating parents. This is a source-level property of n-61b9b3bfb40d, not an inference: its own evolution_init receipt records exactly seven mutation operators - replace_atom, append_atom, delete_atom, insert_atom, change_bond, close_ring, open_ring at weights [0.28, 0.20, 0.16, 0.12, 0.10, 0.08, 0.06] - plus connected-fragment crossover at 0.45 and an optional finishing edit, and not one of them attaches, swaps or deletes a group of atoms. n-cf8d309c06de makes the consequence measurable on the Anchor's own byte-identical output: no trifluoromethyl group and no tetrazole anywhere in 4,350 proposals, and only 12 to 21 distinct Murcko scaffolds in each session's top decile. I recomputed the same limitation directly from this Anchor's own fifteen session logs for this plan: over its 4,350 accepted offspring, the mutation route installs a complete ring system (a ring system present in no generating parent, at least three heavy atoms, carried in as new atoms) in 0 of 2,870 accepted products, and its heavy-atom change from the best generating parent is within one atom in 2,811 of those 2,870 (|delta| >= 2 in 59, 0.0206); all 107 whole-system installations in the whole run come from the crossover route, which can only move a ring system that one of its two parents already had. Round 44 removed the two competing explanations with receipts rather than argument: the selection rule is not the limit (n-5911390da209: six of nine released batches had the entire 160-member field eligible and still failed to improve, and the 17 candidates the restriction would have excluded reached at most 0.943 of the incumbent, none beating it), and the breeding population is not the limit (n-e1a97c9e8713: parents drawn rose from 59.4 to 74.5 distinct skeletons at near-unchanged score while realized increment mass fell 5.978073 to 5.269884). n-8b078abdc05d shows what happens when the lineage tries to reach coarse chemistry by editing instead: the winning edit was a single-atom change in 9,830 of 12,181 replacements and no refined output assembled a new ring system.

adoptions.applicability: Directly applicable here: extraction is offline, in prepare, from the one corpus this benchmark permits, and reads no score, task identity or oracle answer, which is exactly what this position's objective-blindness condition requires. It gives the Anchor access to units its receipt proves it cannot build - trifluoromethyl and tetrazole among them - without any runtime retrieval or library screening.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The offline corpus-mined, frequency-thresholded substructure vocabulary: decompose a corpus into substructures, count them, and keep those occurring more than 1,000 times.

deviations.adopted_setting: The GuacaMol v1 standardized training corpus, all 1,272,851 unique canonical molecules, scanned in file order
deviations.paper_setting: ZINC250k, 195K molecules after removing out-of-vocabulary substructures
deviations.reason: It is the only corpus this benchmark permits, and scanning all of it removes an arbitrary prefix choice and keeps the vocabulary deterministic across replicas; a plan-time probe of the exact decomposition measured 1,121 seconds and 216 kept entries, so the scan fits the 3,600-second prepare timeout and the paper's threshold yields a vocabulary of the same order as its own 82.

deviations.adopted_setting: A unit is a whole ring system (fused or bridged rings merged) or an acyclic side-chain group of two to six heavy atoms; no single-atom entries
deviations.paper_setting: A substructure is a single atom or a single ring
deviations.reason: Single-atom edits already exist in the inherited menu (append_atom, insert_atom, replace_atom), and the registered capability gap is precisely the multi-atom unit and the complete ring system, which a single-ring vocabulary cannot install as one piece.

deviations.adopted_setting: Counted as the number of corpus molecules containing the unit, threshold more than 1,000 molecules
deviations.reason: Counting molecules is unambiguous for a streaming single pass and keeps the threshold reproducible; the value 1,000 is kept at the paper's number rather than tuned.

deviations.adopted_setting: No tree, no network, no extra labels: one uniform draw over the frozen vocabulary inside the inherited genetic loop at 300 accepted observations per task
deviations.paper_setting: A differentiable scaffolding tree with a pretrained GNN knowledge network, 10K-20K precomputed labels and about 5K online oracle calls
deviations.reason: The protocol budget is 300 oracle calls per task and the runtime is offline and task-agnostic; a learned proposal is neither affordable nor identifiable here and would confound the granularity question this ticket asks.

adoptions.implementation_change: prepare() streams the permitted unlabeled corpus once in file order, decomposes each molecule into whole ring systems and 2-to-6-atom acyclic side-chain groups, counts the corpus molecules containing each unit, keeps those above 1,000 that parse back as ordinary neutral connected molecules over the inherited element set with at least one free-hydrogen attachment atom, and writes the kept entries into the prepared artifact beside the inherited configuration.

adoptions.applicability: This is the implementation risk the approach record names, so it is resolved by an explicit rule rather than left to chance: every eligible ring atom of a drawn ring system is a legal attachment point, exactly as the enumeration rule allows, and the product still passes the inherited valence, identity, duplicate and sulfur admission path unchanged.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The attachment-resolution principle DST takes from this work: an atom may attach at any eligible ring atom, two rings may be joined by a bond, and clusters share at most two atoms, with spiro-type products excluded.

deviations.adopted_setting: Draw one legal single-bond attachment uniformly per breeding attempt
deviations.paper_setting: Enumerate all chemically valid attachment configurations and score them with a learned model
deviations.reason: There is no candidate scorer available at this budget, and enumeration per attempt would not fit the per-cell cost; the inherited loop already draws 160 independent candidates per batch, so attachment breadth is bought by sampling rather than by enumeration.

deviations.adopted_setting: Fusion joins are excluded; only single-bond joins are generated, and a whole fused system is installed as one unit instead
deviations.paper_setting: Two rings may also be joined by sharing two atoms and one bond (fusion), and bridged rings are merged
deviations.reason: Fusion requires the junction-tree assembly machinery and its ring-perception edge cases, which is a second mechanism rather than a bounded rule; corpus-mined whole ring systems already supply fused chemistry as single units, so the capability gap is closed without it.

adoptions.implementation_change: GraphOperators.motif_move resolves the attachment explicitly as one new SINGLE bond between a uniformly drawn host atom from the inherited attachment_atoms rule and a uniformly drawn free-hydrogen C/N/O/P/S atom of the drawn unit, decrementing one explicit hydrogen at each site; shared-atom fusion, spiro joins and double or triple joins are not generated at all.

adoptions.applicability: This is the element that distinguishes this arm from the two recorded failures on this lineage: both substituted the operator set, and crossover removal costs -0.014235 to -0.054900 across three Parents, so a replacement here would put a measured-positive component at risk for a question about granularity.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Mixed granularity: atom-level generation is retained and the motif step is added on an already admitted molecule, rather than replacing the atom-level machinery.

deviations.adopted_setting: No model: one operator inside the inherited genetic loop, drawing from a frequency-mined vocabulary
deviations.paper_setting: A pretrained encoder-decoder with a motif vocabulary learned from its training data
deviations.reason: The runtime is offline and task-agnostic with 300 accepted observations per objective; no pretrained generator is registered on this branch and adding one would be a different intervention.

deviations.adopted_setting: Uniform draw over the frozen vocabulary, independent of the host
deviations.paper_setting: Motif choice is conditioned on the partial graph by the decoder
deviations.reason: Any host-conditioned or score-conditioned choice would need a model fitted on accepted labels, which this profile forbids for the vocabulary and which would confound the granularity question; one bound configuration is tested first.

adoptions.implementation_change: Evolution.suggest draws the declared motif probability of 0.30 immediately before the inherited crossover draw of each breeding attempt and applies the motif move to the already scored, already admitted population parent; whenever the draw does not fire or the move cannot complete, control falls through to the unchanged inherited crossover-or-mutation branch, which is therefore the fallback.

adoptions.applicability: It is the independent precedent for the mode pair this ticket's objective asks for - attach, exchange or replace a whole ring system or group - and for keeping that set small; the replace mode is also what keeps the heavy-atom change two-sided instead of monotonically growing molecules toward the 120-atom bound.

deviations.adopted_setting: Uniform draws over modes, units, host sites and motif sites inside the inherited genetic loop; no network and no sampler
deviations.paper_setting: Two pretrained property-agnostic graph neural networks weight the proposal, inside an MCMC sampler

adoptions.applicability: It supports the direction of this intervention at a matched budget inside one optimizer, which is the comparison this lineage has never run; nothing quantitative transfers, because its budget is 10,000 oracle calls per task against this panel's 300.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Fragment-level replacement used explicitly as the mutation operator of a genetic algorithm, with its own ablation ranking fragment-level edits above token- or atom-level edits at a fixed budget.

literature_review.conclusion: The frozen round-45 review r45-bottleneck-move-granularity-admission-and-covariance-uncertainty supplies this position's basis, and I verified the two parts I actually implement against their primary sources this session rather than reusing the summary: DST's vocabulary rule (substructure = atom or single ring, mined from the corpus, kept above 1,000 occurrences, 82 entries on ZINC250k) and its attachment statement (an atom may connect to any ring atom; two rings join by a bond or by sharing two atoms and one bond; spiro and phenalene-like products unsupported), and the JT-VAE assembly step DST defers to, which turns out to be enumeration plus a learned scorer with at most two shared atoms between clusters. That is why the adopted rule is the single-bond case only, drawn uniformly, with fusion and spiro excluded and whole fused ring systems supplied as vocabulary units instead. MIMOSA, searched independently, confirms that a substructure-level step is normally a small closed mode set on the current molecule, which is why this operator has exactly two modes. MoLeR supplies the mixed-granularity shape that keeps the inherited operators as the fallback - the element the two recorded failures on this lineage lacked, since both replaced the operator set. HierVAE supplies the principle that attachment resolution is an explicit step. GenMol supports the direction at a matched budget inside one optimizer while its property-scored dynamic vocabulary is explicitly refused, because scoring a vocabulary by the properties of molecules containing each fragment would read accepted score levels into the generator. PMO bounds the expectation: published rank does not survive a thirty-fold budget change. No reported number is campaign evidence and no effect size transfers to a three-seed, five-task, 300-call panel. Literature origin is not permission to continue: this is one bound configuration with one vocabulary definition, one threshold, one attachment rule, one mode split and one probability, read first on its structural audit against numbers recomputed on this Anchor's own fifteen sessions (0 of 2,870 mutation-route whole-ring-system installations, |delta heavy| >= 2 in 59 of 2,870, accepted median 0.3238) and then on realized incumbent-increment mass against 5.978073 over 253 improvements. If the structural observables move as forecast and realized increments do not rise, move granularity is recorded as refuted for this Anchor and no sweep of the vocabulary, threshold, probability, mode split or attachment heuristic follows.

sources.applicability: This is the only source that states a complete, implementable recipe for the two parts this position needs: an offline frequency-thresholded vocabulary and an explicit attachment rule. Both are corpus-only and run in prepare, so they fit the frozen offline, task-agnostic profile. The differentiable scaffolding tree, the GNN knowledge network and its protocol of 10K-20K precomputed labels plus 5K online calls are incompatible with 300 accepted observations per task and with the rule that no corpus molecule may enter a pool or an evaluation; its reported results are on different tasks and budgets and transfer no effect size.
sources.finding: Read in full this session to fix the exact rule. The vocabulary: substructures are 'either an atom or a single ring'; the authors 'break all the ZINC molecules into substructures (including single rings and single atoms)', count frequencies and 'include the substructures whose frequencies are higher than 1000', which yields 82 substructures including frequent atoms and rings such as benzene. The assembly: 'an atom can be connected to any possible atoms in the ring'; two rings join either '(1) ... a bond (single, double, or triple) to connect the atoms in the two rings' or '(2) ... two rings share two atoms and one bond'; and 'our current setting does not support the spiro compounds' or phenalene-like compounds. Edits are SHRINK, REPLACE and EXPAND on a scaffolding tree, with molecules recovered by enumerating only valid chemical structures.
sources.title: Differentiable Scaffolding Tree for Molecule Optimization (DST)

sources.applicability: It bounds what the enumeration rule actually guarantees, and it is why this position adopts only the single-bond case and refuses the shared-atom fusion case: without the junction-tree machinery and its learned candidate scorer, enumerate-and-score is neither affordable per breeding attempt nor identifiable from 300 accepted labels. One uniform draw over an explicit single-bond rule is the bounded version that is testable now; the pool already supplies 160 independent draws per batch, which is where enumeration breadth comes from here.
sources.finding: Read this session because DST defers its assembly rule to it. The paper assembles 'the molecular graph one neighborhood at a time', enumerates candidate attachments and prunes chemically infeasible combinations (about four candidates per cluster on ZINC after pruning and merging isomorphic ones), constrains any two clusters to share at most two atoms, merges simple rings that share more than two overlapping atoms as bridged compounds, and handles an atom shared by three or more clusters by making that atom its own cluster. There is no closed-form attachment rule: enumeration plus a learned score.
sources.title: Junction Tree Variational Autoencoder for Molecular Graph Generation (JT-VAE)

sources.applicability: Supplies the principle this bottleneck names - a move whose unit is a whole ring system or group, with attachment resolution as an explicit step rather than an afterthought - and it is the recorded root cause of why the round-43 refinement stage could only re-decorate. Its hierarchical encoder-decoder is not adopted: one operator is added to an existing graph-evolution loop.
sources.finding: Carried from the frozen round-45 review: builds molecules from larger, more flexible motifs instead of atoms or small substructures, adding one motif at a time and interleaving motif selection with resolving that motif's attachments, because atom-by-atom generators degrade on larger molecules.
sources.title: Hierarchical Generation of Molecular Graphs using Structural Motifs (HierVAE)

sources.applicability: Gives the exact shape this arm needs: mixed granularity, with the inherited single-atom and bond operators retained as the fallback and the motif step conditioned on an already admitted molecule - here a scored population parent. That matters because both previous coarse-chemistry attempts on this lineage replaced the operator set and lost. Its pretrained model, its corpus and its sampling cost are not adopted and its benchmark position is not campaign evidence.
sources.finding: Carried from the frozen round-45 review: mixes atom-by-atom and motif-by-motif generation with motifs discovered from the training data, decomposes an input molecule into motifs and single atoms, conditions each step on the partial graph so generation can start from a fixed scaffold, and reports comparable unconstrained-optimization results with better scaffold-based results and an order of magnitude faster training and sampling.
sources.title: Learning to Extend Molecular Scaffolds with Structural Motifs (MoLeR)

sources.applicability: Independent confirmation that one substructure-level step is normally defined as a small closed set of modes on an existing molecule, which is why this operator has exactly two: attach and replace. Its pretrained proposal networks are not adopted - 300 accepted observations per task identify none of them and a learned proposal would confound the granularity question - and its delete-only mode is left out because the inherited delete_atom and open_ring already remove at atom granularity and a whole-unit deletion is a separate testable move.
sources.finding: Searched this session as an independent precedent: a substructure-level sampler in which a substructure is either an atom or a single ring and each iteration applies add, replace or delete operations to the current molecule, with the proposal weighted by two property-agnostic pretrained graph networks (topology and substructure type) and candidates kept by multi-constraint weights.

sources.applicability: The only direct matched-budget comparison between a fragment-level and a token- or atom-level edit inside one optimizer, and it points the same way as this campaign's own diagnosis; its honest bound is a margin of about +0.12 sum AUC over 23 tasks, so it supports the direction and supplies no transferable effect size here. Its property-scored, dynamically updated vocabulary is explicitly refused: scoring a vocabulary by the properties of the molecules containing each fragment would read accepted score levels into the generator, which this profile forbids, so the vocabulary here is frequency-based, frozen and objective-blind.

On PMO it reports sum AUC top-10 18.362 against Mol GA 14.708 and Graph GA 13.751, with an ablation of attaching only 17.641, attaching plus token remasking 18.091 and attaching plus fragment remasking 18.208, the stated reason being that each token of a SAFE or SMILES sequence represents a single atom or bond.

sources.applicability: A caution rather than a mechanism, and the reason this is registered as a bounded repertoire extension with its own structural audit instead of an expected win: published rank does not survive a budget change, and this budget is 300 calls per task, thirty times smaller. It also records that assembly granularity is one of the few factors that does matter, which is why the operator-path experiment is worth its position.

hypothesis: Change the unit of one proposal step from a single atom or bond to a whole corpus-frequent substructure: a motif-granularity operation that, with one declared probability, either attaches a drawn ring system or functional group to a scored parent at an explicitly resolved attachment point, or excises one complete ring system or side chain of that parent and installs a drawn one in its place, with the inherited seven atom- and bond-local operators and the connected-fragment crossover retained as the fallback for every attempt the motif path does not take or cannot complete.

finding_summary.headline: Motif moves fired, were admitted and were bought, yet increments fell 5.978 to 5.177 and the panel -0.0534: outcome (d), refuted
finding_summary.insights: The capability gap this lineage has been documenting for three rounds is now closed at the construction and admission layers and proven not to be the binding limit. A move whose unit is a whole ring system can be built, admitted, priced and bought inside this Anchor without breaking a single inherited law - and the search still got worse. That removes move granularity from the list of candidate explanations for this lineage's stalled endpoint gains, in the same way round 44 removed the selection rule and the breeding population, and it does so with the strongest possible version of the supply argument: 30 per cent of attempts, a 245-unit vocabulary containing the exact chemistry the generator could never build, and products admitted at a higher rate than the inherited path's own. The reason the supply did not convert is measurable and it is not about granularity, it is about pricing. The surrogate ranks coarse products systematically below the incumbent's one-atom neighbours (pool mean-rank percentile 0.56 against 0.36) and gives them no uncertainty premium at all (posterior-SD ratio 1.005), so the correlated Thompson draw has no route by which a large structural jump can win a pick on uncertainty. Size is what gets declined: units of nine or more heavy atoms were a third of the supply and a tenth of the purchases, a within-route purchase ratio of 0.32 against 1.33 for small units, which is exactly the shelf the molecular report describes - the bought unit is usually a small group hung on an unchanged skeleton, median five heavy atoms, with only 74 purchases in the whole run exchanging a whole ring system. Where the pricing did buy coarse products in quantity it was badly wrong about them on one objective: 86 per cent of sitagliptin's motif picks landed more than three standard deviations below their predicted mean, and those 88 wasted evaluations plus the declared dilution of crossover exposure from 0.45 to 0.32 of attempts are a sufficient account of that task's 0.19 loss against the law-free reference. A count-fingerprint Tanimoto kernel fitted on 10 to 290 accepted molecules cannot price a one-step multi-atom substitution, and no setting of the motif probability changes that. Two further things the campaign did not know. First, the added operator did move the degeneracy quantity that a richer breeding population failed to move: accepted scores exactly repeating an earlier accepted score fell from 565 to 365, and products scoring exactly their best parent from 205 to 111 - so coarse moves do break the exact-repeat channel, they just do not convert that into mass. Second, the operator is the lineage's first move that can delete a whole ring system, which is the contraction capability the admission-floor arm found missing, but its realized use is still net-growing (median exchange +2 heavy atoms) and the sibling arms' one-sided size diagnosis therefore stands. The method diagnosis from the trajectories is that proposal breadth is no longer the limit; ranking is, and so is the search regime. Mass in the first third of each session rose to 74 per cent from 62 per cent, each cell still converges on a single decorated series, and only 25 of 235 incumbent improvements came from the new route. What this result makes worth trying is a different ranking or surrogate model class - one whose features or kernel can price a fragment-level substitution, or a selection scheme that allocates part of each batch by proposal class rather than by a single posterior ordering - and, separately, a size-matched exchange that swaps a whole fused system for one of comparable size instead of hanging a small group on an intact skeleton. What it does not authorize is any sweep of this vocabulary, its threshold, the 0.30 share, the mode split or the attachment heuristic; the intent said so in advance and the evidence gives no reason to reopen it. One real gap remains in the audit: the registered nitro reading was unreachable because that unit has no free-hydrogen attachment atom under the declared site rule, so the claim that corpus-mined units are the only route to that group is untested here, and the oxidised-sulfur units are effectively unreachable too - the retained sulfur gate rejected 230 of the 236 motif products it refused, all from five such entries.
finding_summary.results: Every structural forecast held, and the endpoint did not. The motif draw fired on 21,969 of 73,510 breeding attempts (0.2989 against the declared 0.30), split 0.4991/0.5009 between attaching a drawn unit and exchanging one of the host's own, and completed a molecule in 96.1 per cent of the attempts it fired on; the 848 failures were all exchange attempts and each one handed the attempt back to the inherited operators. The products were not destroyed at admission - the opposite: 98.8 per cent of them reached the candidate pool against 93.0 per cent for the inherited path, giving a motif-origin pool share of 0.2997 and at least one motif candidate in all 435 announced batches, against the Anchor's exact zero. Whole units really did arrive in one step: in all 343 accepted attach products the heavy-atom change equals the drawn unit's size exactly, 86 per cent of accepted motif products changed size by two or more atoms against the inherited mutation route's 2 per cent, 157 of them installed a complete new ring system (non-zero in all fifteen sessions, and in every case the system installed is the unit drawn) where the inherited mutation route installed none, and the generator produced trifluoromethyl groups (150 accepted molecules) and five-membered four-nitrogen rings (210) for the first time, against zero in all 4,500 of the Anchor's records. The pricing bought them at the pre-registered rate: 746 of 4,350 evaluations were motif-origin, a purchase ratio of 0.572 against the floor of 0.5, with a median accepted score of 0.2468 against the floor of 0.22, and only 97 of 435 batches bought none - not the round-42 declined-supply pattern. Every inherited law held: one configuration identical to the Anchor's apart from the added block, the stall restriction correct in 435 of 435 batches, the sulfur gate and identity admission on every pooled candidate, and the non-motif operator mix within sampling noise of the Anchor's. What did not happen is the gain. Whole-run realized incumbent-increment mass fell to 5.177434 over 235 improvements from the Anchor's 5.978073 over 253, a shortfall of 0.80 against a pre-registered threshold of exceeding it, so the registered falsifier's case (d) - bought and still no gain - applies. The motif route returned 0.117 of that mass from 0.172 of the evaluations; the panel mean came out 0.553654 against 0.607030, a paired delta of -0.053376 with every seed down (-0.0698, -0.0311, -0.0592). The panel figure sits just inside the lower edge of this Anchor's own luck band [-0.055482, +0.014579], so the panel mean alone cannot separate the arm from path luck; the task level can. Against the law-free re-draw on the same Anchor, zaleplon_mpo rose on all three seeds (task mean 0.4781 against 0.4314) and sitagliptin_mpo fell on all three by 0.12, 0.17 and 0.29 (task mean 0.4704 against 0.6620). Sitagliptin is where the operator was most expensive and least useful: it bought 88 of that task's 870 evaluations, none of which beat its generating parent or improved an incumbent, and the surrogate had priced them a median 5.2 standard deviations above what they scored. In the two cells named for tracing, the sitagliptin seed-2 cell that ended at 0.3695 reached its best molecule through a 22-step line of atom-level edits and crossovers with no motif product anywhere in its ancestry, while the median_2 seed-2 cell that ended at 0.2497 does carry four motif products in its ancestry, one of them a small-group exchange in the direct line at evaluation 45 - but every step after it is atom-level work on a fixed tricycle. Cost was never an issue: mining the vocabulary took 735 seconds of a 3,600-second allowance and produced 245 units rather than the planned 216, and the move itself cost 1.3 milliseconds per attempt.

finding:
Every structural forecast held, and the endpoint did not. The motif draw fired on 21,969 of 73,510 breeding attempts (0.2989 against the declared 0.30), split 0.4991/0.5009 between attaching a drawn unit and exchanging one of the host's own, and completed a molecule in 96.1 per cent of the attempts it fired on; the 848 failures were all exchange attempts and each one handed the attempt back to the inherited operators. The products were not destroyed at admission - the opposite: 98.8 per cent of them reached the candidate pool against 93.0 per cent for the inherited path, giving a motif-origin pool share of 0.2997 and at least one motif candidate in all 435 announced batches, against the Anchor's exact zero. Whole units really did arrive in one step: in all 343 accepted attach products the heavy-atom change equals the drawn unit's size exactly, 86 per cent of accepted motif products changed size by two or more atoms against the inherited mutation route's 2 per cent, 157 of them installed a complete new ring system (non-zero in all fifteen sessions, and in every case the system installed is the unit drawn) where the inherited mutation route installed none, and the generator produced trifluoromethyl groups (150 accepted molecules) and five-membered four-nitrogen rings (210) for the first time, against zero in all 4,500 of the Anchor's records. The pricing bought them at the pre-registered rate: 746 of 4,350 evaluations were motif-origin, a purchase ratio of 0.572 against the floor of 0.5, with a median accepted score of 0.2468 against the floor of 0.22, and only 97 of 435 batches bought none - not the round-42 declined-supply pattern. Every inherited law held: one configuration identical to the Anchor's apart from the added block, the stall restriction correct in 435 of 435 batches, the sulfur gate and identity admission on every pooled candidate, and the non-motif operator mix within sampling noise of the Anchor's. What did not happen is the gain. Whole-run realized incumbent-increment mass fell to 5.177434 over 235 improvements from the Anchor's 5.978073 over 253, a shortfall of 0.80 against a pre-registered threshold of exceeding it, so the registered falsifier's case (d) - bought and still no gain - applies. The motif route returned 0.117 of that mass from 0.172 of the evaluations; the panel mean came out 0.553654 against 0.607030, a paired delta of -0.053376 with every seed down (-0.0698, -0.0311, -0.0592). The panel figure sits just inside the lower edge of this Anchor's own luck band [-0.055482, +0.014579], so the panel mean alone cannot separate the arm from path luck; the task level can. Against the law-free re-draw on the same Anchor, zaleplon_mpo rose on all three seeds (task mean 0.4781 against 0.4314) and sitagliptin_mpo fell on all three by 0.12, 0.17 and 0.29 (task mean 0.4704 against 0.6620). Sitagliptin is where the operator was most expensive and least useful: it bought 88 of that task's 870 evaluations, none of which beat its generating parent or improved an incumbent, and the surrogate had priced them a median 5.2 standard deviations above what they scored. In the two cells named for tracing, the sitagliptin seed-2 cell that ended at 0.3695 reached its best molecule through a 22-step line of atom-level edits and crossovers with no motif product anywhere in its ancestry, while the median_2 seed-2 cell that ended at 0.2497 does carry four motif products in its ancestry, one of them a small-group exchange in the direct line at evaluation 45 - but every step after it is atom-level work on a fixed tricycle. Cost was never an issue: mining the vocabulary took 735 seconds of a 3,600-second allowance and produced 245 units rather than the planned 216, and the move itself cost 1.3 milliseconds per attempt.

The capability gap this lineage has been documenting for three rounds is now closed at the construction and admission layers and proven not to be the binding limit. A move whose unit is a whole ring system can be built, admitted, priced and bought inside this Anchor without breaking a single inherited law - and the search still got worse. That removes move granularity from the list of candidate explanations for this lineage's stalled endpoint gains, in the same way round 44 removed the selection rule and the breeding population, and it does so with the strongest possible version of the supply argument: 30 per cent of attempts, a 245-unit vocabulary containing the exact chemistry the generator could never build, and products admitted at a higher rate than the inherited path's own. The reason the supply did not convert is measurable and it is not about granularity, it is about pricing. The surrogate ranks coarse products systematically below the incumbent's one-atom neighbours (pool mean-rank percentile 0.56 against 0.36) and gives them no uncertainty premium at all (posterior-SD ratio 1.005), so the correlated Thompson draw has no route by which a large structural jump can win a pick on uncertainty. Size is what gets declined: units of nine or more heavy atoms were a third of the supply and a tenth of the purchases, a within-route purchase ratio of 0.32 against 1.33 for small units, which is exactly the shelf the molecular report describes - the bought unit is usually a small group hung on an unchanged skeleton, median five heavy atoms, with only 74 purchases in the whole run exchanging a whole ring system. Where the pricing did buy coarse products in quantity it was badly wrong about them on one objective: 86 per cent of sitagliptin's motif picks landed more than three standard deviations below their predicted mean, and those 88 wasted evaluations plus the declared dilution of crossover exposure from 0.45 to 0.32 of attempts are a sufficient account of that task's 0.19 loss against the law-free reference. A count-fingerprint Tanimoto kernel fitted on 10 to 290 accepted molecules cannot price a one-step multi-atom substitution, and no setting of the motif probability changes that. Two further things the campaign did not know. First, the added operator did move the degeneracy quantity that a richer breeding population failed to move: accepted scores exactly repeating an earlier accepted score fell from 565 to 365, and products scoring exactly their best parent from 205 to 111 - so coarse moves do break the exact-repeat channel, they just do not convert that into mass. Second, the operator is the lineage's first move that can delete a whole ring system, which is the contraction capability the admission-floor arm found missing, but its realized use is still net-growing (median exchange +2 heavy atoms) and the sibling arms' one-sided size diagnosis therefore stands. The method diagnosis from the trajectories is that proposal breadth is no longer the limit; ranking is, and so is the search regime. Mass in the first third of each session rose to 74 per cent from 62 per cent, each cell still converges on a single decorated series, and only 25 of 235 incumbent improvements came from the new route. What this result makes worth trying is a different ranking or surrogate model class - one whose features or kernel can price a fragment-level substitution, or a selection scheme that allocates part of each batch by proposal class rather than by a single posterior ordering - and, separately, a size-matched exchange that swaps a whole fused system for one of comparable size instead of hanging a small group on an intact skeleton. What it does not authorize is any sweep of this vocabulary, its threshold, the 0.30 share, the mode split or the attachment heuristic; the intent said so in advance and the evidence gives no reason to reopen it. One real gap remains in the audit: the registered nitro reading was unreachable because that unit has no free-hydrogen attachment atom under the declared site rule, so the claim that corpus-mined units are the only route to that group is untested here, and the oxidised-sulfur units are effectively unreachable too - the retained sulfur gate rejected 230 of the 236 motif products it refused, all from five such entries.

molecular.headline: Aromatic, heavily halogenated small molecules; whole ring systems do get bought, but only small ones, and heteroatom-halogen liabilities dominate.
molecular.overall_character: Across all fifteen cells the generator emits compact drug-sized graphs: the digest counters put ring-closure digits in 96.9-98.7 percent of the 870 proposals per task and lowercase aromatic atoms in 95.98-98.74 percent, with mean SMILES length 43.8-64.1 and no stereocentre markers anywhere (stereocentre_rate 0.0 in all five digests). Reading the trajectory files with RDKit, mean heavy-atom count is 24-36 and mean ring count 2.2-5.0, so the ring chemistry the counters promise is real fused and bicyclic chemistry, not single rings. The declared motif move does appear in what was bought: of the 4350 emitted molecules across the fifteen cells, 746 carry motif provenance in the breed receipts, 334 of those drew a whole ring-system entry and 412 an acyclic group, and 74 replace moves excised a whole ring system from the parent. Intact drawn rings survive into evaluated molecules - a tetrahydrofuran in CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(N(C(=O)C2CCOC2)c2c3c(=O)n(c4ccccc24)C(=O)N(C)C3)c1, a morpholine in CCOc1ccc(N2CCOCC2)cc1C(C)c1c2c(=O)n(c3ccccc13)C(=O)CN(C)C2, an azetidine in CCNCCc1cc(C(CCl)c2cc(Cl)cc(OCCN(C)C)c2)ccc1C1CCN1 and an oxazole in CCSc1cc2c(C(C)(Nc3ncc4nccnc4n3)OC)c(-c3ncco3)c1CO2. But the units that get bought are small: the median drawn entry is 5 heavy atoms and only 77 of the 746 emitted motif products carried a unit of 9 or more heavy atoms, so the vocabulary's large fused entries stay on the shelf. The molecules that top each cell look like the Anchor's: the same tight single-series convergence, the same reliance on N-F, N-Cl, N-Br and O-F decoration in three of the five objectives, and the same complete absence of set stereochemistry. The main visible difference from the Anchor's own cells is where the drift goes when a session stops finding aromatic edits - one cell escalated into bridged saturated polycyclic cages while the Anchor's matching cell stayed aromatic, and one cell collapsed to 19-heavy-atom aminophenol chains where the Anchor's stayed at 34.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-sized bicyclic heteroaromatics, mean 24 heavy atoms and 3.07 ring closures per the digest counters, almost all built as an indole- or pyrazolo-fused ring carrying a 2-position aryl carboxamide: CCc1c2c(C)c(c3[nH]c(C(=O)N(O)c4ccccc4)cc13)N=C2 at 0.5047 and COc1c(C)cc2c(c1CC#N)C=C(C(=O)c1ccccc1)NN2 at 0.4811. Methyl, methoxy, ethyl and acetonitrile decoration on the fused ring; an N-aryl amide head group on every high scorer. The inherited initial record COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC at 0.3051 is already the template, and the optimizer edits its periphery rather than its skeleton.
liabilities: N-halogen amides (N-F, N-Br, N-Cl) throughout, including in the digest best band
free thiophenol S-H appears in 27 of 870 proposals, e.g. Cc1cc2c(c(CC#N)c1C)C=C(C(=O)c1cccc(S)c1)NN2 as the aryl thiol
N-N-S hydrazide-sulfenamide chains such as C=Cc1c(C)c(OC)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)NN(S)c3ccccc3)cc12 in the final band
one- and two-atom degenerate proposals consume oracle calls
missing_features: no dialkylamino ketone or tertiary acetamide side chain; the amide nitrogen is almost always N-aryl or N-halo, never N,N-dialkyl
no halogen-free, all-CHN periphery except in a handful of top molecules; 409 of the 870 proposals carry an N-halogen bond
no pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine-type three-nitrogen fused core; the fused partners are indole, pyrazoline or dihydropyridazine
no set stereochemistry at all (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0) while the proposals average 0.24 unassigned centres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Upward movement is one- and two-atom periphery work on a fixed indole-2-carboxamide: trade a halogen for H, O or a nitrile, keep the anilide. The digest halogen_rate is 0.7448 over the whole proposal set, yet the single best molecule carries no halogen at all and uses an N-hydroxy anilide instead, while the N-bromo/N-chloro variant COc1c(C)c(C)cc2c1C(C(=O)N(Br)c1ccccc1)C(Cl)N2C#N sits lower at 0.4734. Molecules stripped to one or two atoms score exactly zero (OF, worst band).

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the panel: mean SMILES length 64.1, max 152, digest ring-closure rate 0.9874 and RDKit mean 5.0 rings. Two distinct series. One is a 2-aminopteridine (Nc1ncc2nccnc2n1) tied through a benzylic quaternary carbon to a methoxy- and thioether-rich benzene: COCSc1cc(OC)c(C(C)(Nc2ncc3nccnc3n2)OC)c(OC)c1CF at 0.6366 and the dioxole-fused COc1cc2sc3c(c2c(C)c1C(Nc1ncc2nccnc2n1)OC)CO3. The other, in a different seed, is a polyaryl aryl-ketone-linked pyridazine bearing difluoromethoxy pyrimidines and N-linked azoles, e.g. Cc1cc(C(=O)c2cc(-n3ccc4cncnc43)c(C)cc2C(C)C(C)C)ncc1N(C)c1nc(OC(F)F)ncc1C.
liabilities: alpha-halo aminal and alpha-halo ether carbons: 179 of 870 proposals carry N-C-halogen, e.g. COc1c2c(SC(Cl)OC)c(C)c(c1C(C)(Nc1ncc3nccnc3n1)OC)OC2
benzylic quaternary carbons bearing two oxygens and a nitrogen are stacked repeatedly, giving mean QED 0.28 over the task set
tetrazole-fused and polyazole-dense products such as C=Cc1cc(C(=O)c2cc(-n3ncnn3)ccc2C)nnc1-n1ccc2nnnnc21 pile up ring nitrogens with no carbon spacer
missing_features: no sulfonamide or any sulfonyl linker: only 3 of the 870 proposals contain S(=O)(=O)N at all
no basic saturated amine ring (piperazine appears once in 870) to carry the aryl-ether end of the molecule
no H-bond-donating amide NH on the aromatic core in the top band; the high scorers use ethers and thioethers only
no fused tricyclic drawn from the vocabulary reaches the top band, although the vocabulary contains 10- and 13-heavy-atom fused entries
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The visible gradient is narrow (digest span 0.5 to 0.6366) and is driven by keeping a fixed aminopyrimidine-fused bicycle and its aryl partner while shuffling small substituents - SCH2OCH3 for SCH3, OCH3 for CH3, CF3 for H. Nothing in the band changes the skeleton; the worst band is single atoms and diatomics (FBr) that all sit at the 0.5 floor, so skeleton loss is penalised while periphery churn is nearly free.

per_task.generated_character: The least ring-dense set of the five: digest ring-closure rate 0.9874 but RDKit mean only 2.23 rings and mean fused-system size 1.05, i.e. mostly isolated benzene rings joined by flexible chains. Every high scorer is a bis-basic-amine: a secondary N-ethylamine chain on one ring and a dimethylaminoethyl ether or chain on the other, e.g. CCNCCc1cc(C(N)(Cl)c2cccc(CCN(C)C)c2)cc(O)c1Cl at 0.9964 and the tetrahydroisoquinoline-bearing CCNCCc1cc(C(N)(Cl)c2ccc3c(c2)CCN(C)C3)cc(O)c1Cl. One session shrank instead of growing: its top molecules are 16-19 heavy-atom single-ring aminophenols such as NCCCNCCc1cc(O)cc(Cl)c1 and CC(C)CCNCCc1cc(O)cc(O)c1.
liabilities: alpha-chloro carbinamine C(N)(Cl) at the benzylic junction of the best molecules - an unisolable chloro-aminal
free aryl thiol S-H, e.g. NCCc1cc(S)c(Cl)c(CCNCCCC(N)N)c1 in the final band
geminal diamine chains such as CC(C)CCNCCc1cc(O)cc(O)c1 are fine, but 39 of 870 proposals carry N-C-N aminals
one session degenerated to flexible polyamines of 16-19 heavy atoms with a single aromatic ring
missing_features: the basic nitrogens are almost always acyclic: ring-embedded basic N appears in 34 of 870 proposals, and piperazine never
no aryl-piperazine or aryl-piperidine linkage, the ordinary way this chemistry is written
no amide or sulfonamide linker in the high band at all; the two aryl groups are joined by a single sp3 carbon
no specified configuration at the benzylic linking carbon although it is a stereocentre in every top molecule
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient tracks basic nitrogen count and a meta-substituted phenol, not size. The top band averages 2.2-2.5 basic amine centres against 1.37 over the whole set, while the worst band is the sulfonamide-bearing proline amides inherited from the initial pool, e.g. CC(CC(=O)O)NC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.0007 - acid plus sulfonamide and no basic centre scores near zero.

per_task.generated_character: The most saturated, least halogenated set: digest halogen_rate 0.1 against 0.49-0.74 elsewhere, ring-closure rate 0.9851, RDKit mean 4.98 rings and 1.8 unassigned stereocentres per molecule. The whole task converges on one architecture: a benzo-fused lactam-imide tricycle carrying an N-methyl piperazinone or tetrahydropyrazinone ring, with a 4-ethoxy-3-propylphenyl group on the other side. Seed 2 is the clearest case - CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2c3c(=O)n(c4ccccc24)C(=O)CCN(C)C3)c1 at 0.2497 and its ring-contracted sibling CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2c3c(=O)n(c4ccccc24)CCN(C)C3)c1 at 0.2464, both reached by atom-level insert and delete steps on a crossover product. This is the only task where ring-embedded basic nitrogen is common: 350 of 870 proposals, piperazine in 43.
liabilities: 60 of 870 proposals carry acyclic N-C-N aminals, e.g. CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(N(c2c3c(=O)n(c4ccccc24)C(=O)N(C)C3)C2CNC2)c1 attaches an azetidine through an aminal-like N
bridged and spiro growth creeps in: 65 percent of seed-2 proposals carry a bridgehead atom and about half a seven-membered ring, lifting mean SA score to 4.0-4.7
strained three- and four-membered rings attached to amide nitrogens are frequent in the mid band
missing_features: no sulfonyl group anywhere near the top: 8 of 870 proposals contain S(=O)(=O) and none of them in a high band
no methylenedioxyphenyl or other fused dioxole on the pendant aryl, only simple ethoxy and propyl
no set configuration at the two ring-fusion carbons that every top molecule carries as unassigned centres
no pyrazolo-pyrimidinone-type all-nitrogen fused heteroaromatic; the fused cores are carbocyclic-benzo plus lactam
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Upward steps are ring-size and linker surgery inside a fixed tricycle: aryl directly bonded beats aryl-N and aryl-CH(CH3) linkage (0.2448 and 0.2299 against 0.2497), and inserting one CH2 into the lactam ring is worth the last step. Alkoxy-aryl identity is held constant across the whole top band; the worst band is C#C and single atoms at 0.0, so the gradient rewards keeping the whole assembly intact.

per_task.generated_character: The widest score span in the digest (4.3e-44 to 0.5495) and the most chemically strained set. Two seeds produced fluorinated xanthine-like fused pyrimidinediones bearing an N-aryl phenol: Cn1c(=O)n(F)c(=NN2C=C2)c2c(CCF)n(-c3cc(OF)c(F)cc3O)cc21 at 0.5495 and CC=C(C)c1c2c(=O)n(O)c(=O)n(C)c2c(F)n1C1C=C(F)CN=C1F at 0.4923. The third seed went somewhere else entirely: its molecules are bridged saturated polycyclic cages fused to an N-fluoro benzoxazinone, N=C1N(F)C(=O)C2=C3CN(c4cc5ccc4N(F)OC5=O)C2N1CC1=CCC=C13 at 0.3695 and CN1OC(=O)c2cc(F)c1c(N1C3=C4C(=O)N(F)C(=N)N(CC5=CCC=C53)C41)c2 at 0.3634. That cell averages 7.0 rings, a bridgehead atom in 90 percent of proposals, a seven-membered ring in 80 percent, only 1.45 aromatic rings and mean SA score 5.5 (6.1 in its own top band) - against 3.0-3.9 rings and 2.2-2.7 aromatic rings in the other two seeds. Its skeleton came from a run of close_ring and crossover steps on an early benzodioxolone, not from the motif path, which contributed none of that cell's top band.
liabilities: N-F and O-F bonds in the digest best band and in 166 and 197 of 870 proposals respectively - not isolable chemistry
azirine and cyclopropenyl-imine fragments: a three-membered N-containing unsaturated ring appears in 17 percent of one seed's proposals
218 of 870 proposals carry an aminal N-C-N, and the cage series carries two per molecule
the cage cell's mean SA score 5.5 with bridgeheads and seven-membered rings is the least makeable chemistry on the panel
ring N-O bonds in 32 percent of the cage cell's proposals
missing_features: no aryl CF3 and essentially no CF3 at all (2 of 870 proposals); fluorine is delivered as N-F (166) and O-F (197) instead
no trifluoromethyl-substituted fused triazole; the fused partners are pyrimidinedione and cyclopentene-bridged cages
no free primary amine beta to an aryl ring: only 13 of 870 proposals carry an unacylated primary amine
no set configuration anywhere, although the cage products carry several ring-fusion stereocentres
no trifluorophenyl-type all-carbon fluoroaryl ring; aromatic rings carry OH, OF and single F
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Where the molecules stay aromatic the gradient tracks fluorine count and an intact N-aryl phenol: the digest top band carries 2.5-4.0 fluorines per molecule and a heteroatom-bound F in nearly every molecule, while the near-zero worst band is fluorine-only diatomics (FS) and oversized dimers. In the cage cell the same upward steps add F to the cage and close another ring, so its gradient rewards fluorination of an increasingly saturated and bridged skeleton rather than of an aromatic one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: RDKit substructure counts over the fifteen trajectory files give 409 of 870 proposals with an N-halogen bond in one session set and 197 of 870 with an O-halogen bond in another; the digest best band of two objectives contains N-F, N-Br and O-F molecules, and the digest halogen_rate is 0.72-0.74 there.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator forms halogen bonds to nitrogen and oxygen as freely as to carbon, and these appear in its own highest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A proposal-time structural filter that forbids a halogen bonded to N, O or S would remove this whole class without any objective knowledge, and would force the same fluorine-adding pressure onto carbon, where the generator currently almost never places it (2 of 870 CF3 groups in the set where fluorine mattered most).

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 4350 emitted molecules, 746 carry motif provenance, median drawn unit 5 heavy atoms, and only 77 carried a unit of 9 or more heavy atoms; just 74 replace moves excised a whole ring system from the parent, so the usual outcome is a small group hung on an unchanged skeleton, as in the attached tetrahydrofuran and morpholine products.
transferable_gaps.gap: Multi-atom moves pay out only in small units; whole fused ring systems are drawn but almost never survive to evaluation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A unit-level move needs a size-matched exchange path - excise one whole fused ring system and install another of comparable size - plus admission that does not treat a large single-step change as a loss, otherwise the repertoire extension collapses back onto one-atom-equivalent edits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in all five digests, while RDKit finds 0.24-1.98 unassigned chiral centres per molecule across the trajectories, including at the ring-fusion and benzylic carbons of every top molecule on three objectives.
transferable_gaps.gap: No molecule the generator proposes has a specified configuration, though most carry unassigned stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The graph representation carries no stereo tag and no operator sets one. Adding configuration as a mutable attribute, with an operator that flips it, would open a dimension the generator presently cannot search at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-embedded basic N appears in 350 of 870 proposals on one objective but only 19-34 of 870 on three others, and piperazine appears once or never there; yet one digest best molecule carries a fused tetrahydroisoquinoline N-methyl amine and the attached-azetidine product shows the move is reachable.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basic nitrogen is almost never placed inside a ring, although ring-embedded basic amines appear in the generator's own best molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Saturated N-heterocycles exist in the vocabulary but are not preferentially installed at carbon sites bearing acyclic amines. A move that cyclises an existing acyclic amine chain into a ring, or that swaps an acyclic amine for a ring-embedded one, would supply this in a task-blind way.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One session's proposals average 7.0 rings with a bridgehead atom in 90 percent, a seven-membered ring in 80 percent, 1.45 aromatic rings and mean SA score 5.5 rising to 6.1 in its own top band, against 3.0-3.9 rings and SA 3.8-3.9 in the matched sessions; the cage skeleton was built by a run of close_ring and crossover steps.
transferable_gaps.gap: Repeated ring-closing drives saturated bridged polycyclic cages with no counter-pressure, losing aromatic character and makeability.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring-closure operators are unconstrained with respect to bridging and fusion depth. A bound on new bridgehead atoms or on ring count per molecule, or an aromatic-content-preserving variant of ring closure, would stop a stalled session from walking out of makeable space.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest worst band contains molecules such as C, N, F, OF, FF, FBr, C#C and CCl, scored at or near the floor on four objectives; these are emitted proposals, not initial records.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits one- and two-atom fragments that cannot carry any chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A minimum heavy-atom admission bound at proposal time, phrased on the graph alone, would return those evaluations to the search without any objective knowledge.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 11 of 4350 emitted molecules drew a sulfonyl or sulfonamide unit from the vocabulary, and none of them reached any cell's top band; three objectives' proposal sets contain 8 or fewer S(=O)(=O) groups in 870 molecules, while the one objective whose initial records already carried sulfonamides retained 115.
transferable_gaps.gap: Oxidised-sulfur chemistry is reachable but effectively unused.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Oxidised-sulfur centres survive mainly by inheritance from the starting records, not by construction. A proposal path that can build a sulfonyl or sulfonamide centre de novo, and admission that does not treat a new sulfur signature as a regression, would make this class reachable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each cell's top band is one scaffold with periphery variation - a single aminopteridine-benzene series, a single indole-2-carboxamide series, a single benzo-fused lactam-imide series - and the ancestry of the best molecule in two traced cells is a chain of one-atom edits and crossovers on one skeleton for the last 150 evaluations.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within a session the generator converges on a single decorated series and stops changing skeletons.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Parent selection and admission reward local periphery edits over skeleton change, so late budget is spent inside one neighbourhood. A diversity-aware parent pool or a skeleton-level acceptance path would let a session hold more than one architecture at once.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
